text:
marta: Heads up — noticed customers getting 429s but no RateLimit-* headers in responses for a subset of routes after last night's policy rollout. Can someone check routing rewrite rules?
josh: Ack. I saw one affected tenant where client-side retry logic kept hammering. Seems like our dynamic rewrite policy stripped headers when we applied 'strip-sensitive' on the response path.
annika: Which policy ID? I didn't touch rate-limit logic.
marta: policy id dyn-rewrite-v2. It's the one that conditionally strips X-Internal-* and also normalizes query keys. I think the rule that collapses duplicate query params runs before we attach quota headers.
ryan: Oof ordering bug then. We attach quota headers in the rate-limit filter which expects the original path/query. If query normalization runs first and collapses a token param, the quota key lookup misses and we fall back to global rate limiter (and then we strip the RateLimit-* headers later).
josh: Repro steps I ran: curl -i "https://api.redwood/test?tenant=acme&session=abc&session=abc" -H 'x-client-id: acme'  — when policy order was wrong I saw 429 with no RateLimit-Remaining/Reset.
annika: Can you paste the policy snippet? I want to propose a minimal fix.
marta: Paste below (from the gateway config):
```json
{
  "policies": [
    {"id":"dyn-rewrite-v2","stage":"response","rules":[{"type":"strip_headers","match":"X-Internal-*"},{"type":"strip_headers","match":"RateLimit-*","when":"tenant_internal"}]},
    {"id":"query-normalize","stage":"request","rules":[{"type":"dedupe_query","keys":["session","token"]},{"type":"lowercase_keys"}]}
  ]
}
```
josh: Two issues: 1) We should never strip RateLimit-* headers in response stage (we only do that for infra->client cases, not client-facing routes). 2) Query normalization must run before quota lookup in request stage, or quota lookup must be resilient to normalized keys.
ryan: Suggestion: add an explicit attach-rate-limit policy that runs in response after rate-limit filter, with a guard to only add headers if present from rate limiter. That way even if some earlier strip runs we re-insert them (but re-inserting is a bit gross). Better: change ordering so rate-limit filter runs after request normalize and before any response-strip.
annika: I prefer reorder + guard. Re-inserting creates mismatch risk between telemetry and headers. If a proxy adds headers after enforcement, telemetry will still show original enforcement but client sees something else.
marta: Agreed. Also we need telemetry: mark rewrite-policy-used tag on the span so we can correlate missing headers to policy runs.
ingest-bot: trace created -> span_id: abc123, tags: [route: /test, policy: dyn-rewrite-v2, trace_mode: replay]
josh: Ops plan: 1) revert dyn-rewrite-v2 response rule that strips RateLimit-* (canary to 2% of traffic), 2) reorder query-normalize to run before quota lookup, 3) add a unit test to the gateway that simulates duplicate query keys and asserts quota header presence.
annika: I'll open a PR for policy ordering + tests. Marta can you do the canary config?
marta: On it. Patching config now, will push canary at 02:10 UTC. deploy-bot: deploy queued by marta for gateway-configs at 02:10 UTC — canary targets: us-west-2:2%
ryan: Add a dashboard check: alert if >0.5% of 429 responses lack RateLimit-Remaining header in the canary traffic.
josh: I'll add the alert and a quick grafana panel showing header-presence ratio by route.
marta: Thanks. Follow-up: let's also add a lint rule to disallow stripping RateLimit-* in response policies unless explicitly allowed. Prevents accidental regressions.
annika: +1, will add to linter.
ryan: Cool — track in #eng-platform postmortem if anything pops up.
marta: Closing thread once canary looks good. Will update here with timestamps and metrics. :thumbsup:
